why: next@16.3.3+ and sharp@0.35.4 cleared the two next RCE advisories (GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36, GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4) and the sharp/libheif advisory (GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c) — real patch-version bumps, not baselined. maplibre-gl's GHSA-jrc7-96c5-q579 (DOM.sanitize() XSS in the attribution control, aka CVE-2026-85061) was previously baselined here because the installed 4.7.1 predated the vulnerable code (sanitize() was only added in 5.0.0, so 4.7.1 sat inside the advisory's stated '<= 6.4.0' range without containing the flaw). That baseline is gone as of 2026-09-23: maplibre-gl was bumped straight to 6.4.1, the actual fixed version, so the entry is removed rather than carried forward stale. 6.4.1 was chosen deliberately over any 5.0.0-6.4.0 version, since per the code-history analysis above those versions ARE genuinely vulnerable — re-verify this reasoning before ever downgrading maplibre-gl. picomatch (added 2026-11-17, removed 2026-11-18): GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf / CVE-2026-112366 (ReDoS through single-branch repeated extglobs, published 2026-10-19) was WITHDRAWN by GitHub on 2026-11-18 (advisory updated 15:38:58Z, title now reads 'Withdrawn Advisory: …'), so npm audit stopped reporting it at any version while the lockfile still resolves picomatch@4.0.7 — the gate's stale-entry check failed on every pull_request merge ref until the entry was deleted, the same withdrawal shape as braces in the mobile baseline (2026-10-23). At acceptance time the reasoning was: 4.0.7 was npm's dist-tag latest with no first_patched_version published, the copy the gate counted was the production top-level picomatch@4.0.7 (a second 2.3.2 nested under micromatch is dev-flagged and outside --omit=dev), picomatch arrived only transitively via vite, @rollup/pluginutils, @rollup/plugin-commonjs, tinyglobby and @parcel/watcher file-matching tooling, and no source file under src/ or app/ imports it. Accepted as unfixable then, not as harmless — if GitHub re-publishes the advisory, this red returns with the same reasoning attached.
